artifacts.summary: Narrowed the sapience MCP write-tool grant from 11 to 7 entries and reconciled eleven coupled surfaces across the sapience and core source stores; fresh-load and scoped-gate verification both confirmed.

completion_data.completion_summary: Removed the four MCP write-tool grants from agent-system/extensions/sapience/settings-fragment.json (11 -> 7 entries) and brought every surface that stated the old grant figure as current fact into agreement across five phases: verify-sapience-mcp.sh's probe, core's carve-out worked example and its cross-reference, the write-path rule's landed disposition, review-gate-boundary.md's grant disclosure, and the extension's remaining metadata/merge-source files. A scratch-repo fresh load confirmed exactly 7 grants with no write tool; this repository's own pre-existing 11-grant merge residual is recorded explicitly, not silently left implying full closure.

memory_candidates.content: When narrowing a permission-grant count that multiple prose surfaces cite by figure (not just the two files a dispatch names), each source-store edit that shrinks or regenerates a cited file can itself trigger a doc-lint/index-line-count failure in a scoped verification gate (verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 3,4 doc-lints the WHOLE extensions tree, not just the files touched this phase) -- both a deployed-vs-source drift check (any edited script/rule/context file not yet redeployed) and an index-entries.json line_count mismatch (any edited markdown file whose line count the index tracks). Rather than deferring all redeployment to a single final phase, running an idempotent deploy-headless.sh pass (and generate-context-line-counts.sh --write when a markdown file's size changed) after each intermediate phase lets that phase's own named scoped gate pass as literally written, at near-zero marginal cost since the deploy and the line-count regeneration are both idempotent.

To verify a 'fresh extension load produces grant set X' acceptance criterion without polluting the current repository's own merged settings (which may carry a pre-existing additive-merge residual from before a narrowing), drive the extension manager's Lua API directly in a throwaway scratch git repo: `nvim --headless -c "lua local ext_config = require('neotex.plugins.ai.shared.extensions.config'); local ext_init = require('neotex.plugins.ai.shared.extensions.init'); local manager = ext_init.create(ext_config.claude()); local ok, err = manager.load('EXTNAME', { project_dir = 'SCRATCH_DIR', confirm = false }); print(ok)" -c "qa!"`. This writes only into SCRATCH_DIR's own .claude/ and .claude-extensions.json, never touching the real repo's ~/.claude.json project registry (confirmed: no scratch-repo key appeared there). Precedent for this call pattern already existed in test-mcp-merge-target.sh's run_lua/do_load helpers.
